title: Aequitas: A Bias and Fairness Audit Toolkit
explain_beginner: This paper introduces Aequitas, a free tool that helps check whether artificial intelligence systems treat different groups of people fairly. It can look at groups based on things like race, gender, or religion. The authors note that many ways to measure fairness exist, but people often do not agree on which one to use, and few practical tools are available. Aequitas lets users test a model against several fairness measures for different groups. This matters because AI is used in decisions that affect people, and without regular checks, it may unintentionally harm some groups. The tool aims to make fairness checks easier and more common.
explain_business: This paper describes Aequitas, a free open source tool for checking whether an AI system treats different groups fairly. It lets teams test models against multiple fairness measures for groups such as race, gender, or religion. The authors say that although many fairness measures exist, organizations often lack a standard way to apply them. Aequitas is designed to fit into normal machine learning work. In practice, it gives leaders a way to add fairness checks before deploying AI that makes decisions about people. That can inform decisions about whether and how to deploy a model, and it supports more equitable choices.
explain_practitioner: The authors present Aequitas, an open source toolkit for auditing machine learning models for bias and fairness. It plugs into an existing machine learning workflow and lets users compute several fairness metrics across multiple population subgroups. The work addresses a practical gap: many fairness definitions and bias metrics exist, but there is little agreement on which to choose and few resources to apply them. Aequitas makes these checks easier and repeatable. Its key contribution is operationalizing group fairness testing so data scientists, researchers, and policymakers can compare model behavior across subgroups and make more informed decisions about deploying algorithmic systems.
